environmentNote: Real Postgres reachable this session; all DB-backed claims verified against a real database, not merely reasoned about.
positiveFindings: Cross-instrument double-counting is structurally prevented (instrumentId is a scalar FK confined to base-document-defining types; cross-cutting documents relate only via DocumentRelationshipEdge).
An amendment uploaded before its base document is handled gracefully (resolvePackageRelationships is order-independent, returns UNRESOLVED/REVIEW_REQUIRED, never a crash or a guess).

All four effective-dating consumers (covenant-engine.ts, service.ts, solver/coverage.ts, amendment/operative-state.ts) are genuinely consistent: closed-open [effectiveFrom, effectiveTo), both-null=always-effective, verified at the source-text level (actual lte/gt and </>= operators pattern-matched, not just behaviorally inferred).

Same-day-amendment conflicts correctly detected (AMENDMENT_CONFLICT) and propagate to OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED, never silently resolved by iteration order at the STATUS level (currentText itself is a separate, lower-severity finding - see AMENDMENT_OPERATIVE_STATE_ASSURANCE).
Null/unresolvable effective dates never treated as already-effective; retroactive and future-dated amendments both resolve correctly relative to a query date.

The forward provenance chain (DiscoveredCandidate -> CovenantContextBundle) is real and complete: discoveryId, structuralNodeIds, sourceCitation, discoveryRunVersion, originatingDiscoveryId, retrievalAlgorithmVersion, contentIdentity all present and correct.
reviewCandidate() genuinely refuses to alter a decision once ExtractionCandidate.promotedAt is set - 'a promoted candidate's review decision is final' is real, not aspirational.

The Phase 3D semantic-precedent store's supersedePrecedent never mutates in place; superseded precedent is excluded from listings by default - a real positive precedent for staleness-safety, though in-memory-only and not yet reachable from any product surface.

findings.title: Real, wired onboarding upload action bypasses all content-hash dedup, creating duplicate Document rows for identical files
findings.reproduction: app/[companyId]/onboarding/documents/actions.ts:16 calls lib/onboarding/documents.ts's uploadAndChunkDocument directly - zero content-hash check anywhere. A dedup-safe wrapper (lib/connectors/upload-connector.ts's uploadDocumentThroughIngestion) exists, is tested, and correctly refuses a second Document row for identical bytes - but nothing in the real UI path calls it.

findings.title: persistStructuralNodes never deletes stale DocumentNode rows after a legitimate re-extraction
findings.reproduction: Re-running STRUCTURE over the same documentId with corrected charStart values does not update the old row - it silently adds a second one, both returned together by every real documentNode.findMany({where:{documentId}}) call site, nothing marks either as current. Low-blast-radius today only because DocumentNode has near-zero real population (2 rows in the whole live database).

findings.title: Document.supersedesDocumentId is populated but never consulted by any amendment-precedence or calculation logic
findings.reproduction: covenant-engine.ts's real effectiveDateFilter references only effectiveFrom/effectiveTo. The field's only real reader (canonical-state.ts:147) uses it solely for a display count. The Roadmap's characterization of this field as 'genuinely used by the legacy production engine today' overstates its role.

findings.title: resolveEffectiveDate classifies an amendment as EXPLICIT_EFFECTIVE_DATE even when the same sentence conditions effectiveness on unsatisfied conditions precedent
findings.reproduction: 'This Amendment shall become effective as of December 1, 2023, subject to the satisfaction of the following conditions precedent...' is classified EXPLICIT_EFFECTIVE_DATE with a concrete, immediately-applicable date. The identical conditional language WITHOUT a date is correctly caught as CONDITIONAL_UNRESOLVED, isolating the gap to 'date present + condition present'. independent-verification.ts contains zero references to conditions/effective dates, so nothing downstream catches this. This is the inverse of Invariant #13's concern: here, not-yet-effective language silently appears current.

findings.title: Individual ContextItems lose their originating discoveryId once separated from their containing CovenantContextBundle - already exercised by a live consumer
findings.reproduction: A real CovenantContextBundle built via the unmodified buildCovenantContextBundle has bundle.originatingDiscoveryId present and correct, but no item in bundle.items[] carries a discoveryId/bundleId property. semantic/tools.ts's summarizeItem() (line 59) already hands the LLM a bare summary stripped of bundle context. Primary source-citation (Invariant #1) is intact (sourceCitation/documentId present) - this is loss of the secondary 'which discovery run produced this' audit trail, not a citation-integrity break.

findings.title: Document.typeConfirmedByUser/amendmentRelationshipConfirmedByUser default to true at the DB-column level with no code-level guardrail against a future creation path omitting the override
findings.reproduction: A bare prisma.document.create() with no confirmation flags produces a row that reads as fully human-confirmed with zero review. package-graph/persistence.ts's real classification-write guard trusts this flag completely. Every currently-wired code path correctly overrides this to false - no reachable defect today, but a landmine for a future connector or bulk-import script that doesn't know the convention.

findings.title: No review/approval-consuming code re-validates a stored confirmation or reviewStatus flag against document supersession or extraction-version identity
findings.reproduction: package-graph/persistence.ts's typeConfirmedByUser gate and lib/onboarding/review.ts confirmed to reference neither supersedesDocumentId nor any extraction-version field. Currently more theoretical than reachable since FA-DOCID-02 established there is no real in-place re-extraction concept.
